meta.title: Languages by Country (ranked) x Resources
meta.grain: one row per country x language
meta.ranking: By how many DX people groups claim it as their PRIMARY language in that country.
meta.bridge_caveat: bridge_candidate = primary to MORE THAN ONE group here. That is NOT a national trade language: a lingua franca no unengaged group claims as primary is invisible to this method (Urdu in Pakistan is the clearest case). See gaps-and-opportunities.bridge_strength before acting.

source.definition: A BRIDGE CANDIDATE is a language that is the primary language of MORE THAN ONE distinct DX people group in that country — measured from the corpus, not asserted from a list.
source.honest_limit: This is NOT the same as a national trade language. It finds languages widely used AMONG THE UNENGAGED GROUPS TRACKED HERE, and will MISS a lingua franca that no unengaged group claims as primary (e.g. Hindi in India). Named bridge_candidates, not trade_languages, for that reason.
source.why_not_a_list: restcountries v3.1 is DEPRECATED (returns an error body); Ethnologue is paywalled; Glottolog has no lingua-franca field. Hand-typing 175 national languages from memory is exactly where a confident error would enter.
